properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 20 at 2:22PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Yap State with a few areas of stronger
gusts north of Faraulep.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. By
midweek, models indicate the potential for a circulation to slowly
organize as it passes between Yap and Guam into the Philippine Sea.
As this happens, westerly winds and gusts will increase with showers
and thunderstorms. While these conditions will generally be felt
across Yap State, portions of the Republic of Palau could see heavy

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 19 at 11:59AM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
ESFRIW

Periods of showers and thunderstorms are expected across the northern
half of Wyoming Saturday and Sunday as a wet weather system shifts
east across the state. This weather system is funneling abundant
tropical moisture into northern and eastern portions of the state
with it's eastward progression. Given the high moisture content, many
thunderstorms could feature heavy rainfall and possibly lead to
localized flooding. Poor drainage areas, urban areas, and steep
terrain will be the most susceptible locations for this isolated
flooding.

Many locations could see an additional 0.5" to 1.25" of rain through
Sunday afternoon, with a majority of this rain falling quickly in
thunderstorms.

Remember, if you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around don't down!

NWSheadline: Showers and Thunderstorms Could Produce Heavy Rainfall and Localized Flooding through Sunday
